proposed_source.title: Danny Calegari, Introduction to Knot Theory, full 48-page course notes
proposed_source.locator: Example 1.10 and Proposition 1.11, printed/PDF p. 8, plus the opening comparison on p. 9; §4.1, pp. 30–34 (prime coloring equation, local invariance and explicit trefoil matrix); §4.2, pp. 34–37, ending before §4.3 (presentations, abelianization and the dihedral representation interpretation).

contents.name: Example 1.10 and Proposition 1.11, p. 8: tricoloring definition, local invariance and the counts tau_3(unknot)=3 and tau_3(right-handed trefoil)=9
contents.reason: Directly supports the worked trefoil/unknot count example. The source states the counts and sketches local move checks; the actual local item verifies all nine trefoil assignments and three unknot assignments using its proved suppliers.

contents.name: Opening comparison on p. 9: one tricoloring invariant does not decide whether the unknot and figure-eight are equivalent
contents.reason: Independent treatment of the limits of one coloring invariant. The assigned counterexample uses a different explicit pair and prime (trefoil and unknot at p=5), proved locally with a separate p=3 count and group distinction; this source passage is context, not that exact witness.

contents.name: §4.1, pp. 30–32: Fox p coloring equation x_under1+x_under2=2x_over and unique local extensions across R1, R2 and R3
contents.reason: Supports the actual finite linear system and coloring interpretation used by both B items. The full local invariance proof is supplied in the assigned theorem rather than deferred to a source diagram.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 32, Example 4.1: every 2-coloring of a knot is monochromatic
contents.reason: The two assigned B items use odd primes 3 and 5; adding a separate even-prime example is unnecessary for their approved computations.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 32: the explicit coloring matrix for knot 7_3 and its determinant 13
contents.reason: This is a different knot and would expand the approved B inventory beyond the fixed trefoil/unknot worked case and boundary counterexample.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 33, Lemma 4.2: oddness of the knot determinant from colorings modulo 2
contents.reason: The assigned proofs directly row-reduce their finite Fox systems and do not need a general determinant theorem.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 33: claimed formula n_p=1+nu_p(Delta) from determinant prime multiplicity
contents.reason: No determinant-valuation shortcut is imported. Valuation alone need not equal nullity modulo a prime: the matrix [9] has nullity 1 modulo 3 but 3-adic valuation 2. The local counts at primes 3 and 5 are independently computed directly.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 33, Exercise 4.3: the t-coloring and Alexander-polynomial construction
contents.reason: The assigned examples concern ordinary dihedral Fox colorings, not the general t parameter or Alexander-polynomial construction.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 34: right-handed trefoil matrix and Delta(t)=t^2-t+1, with Delta(-1)=3
contents.reason: The displayed matrix at t=-1 gives the same three Fox equations used locally. Direct rank calculations give nine colorings at p=3 and five at p=5. The source does not itself state the full trefoil/unknot counterexample at p=5, so no such source claim is invented.

contents.name: §4.1, p. 34: figure-eight matrix and Delta(t)=t^2-3t+1, including a nontrivial 5-coloring
contents.reason: The current B items do not compute the figure-eight. Its distinct matrix is not substituted for the fixed trefoil witness.

contents.name: §4.2, pp. 34–36: diagram meridian presentation and local Tietze transformations under Reidemeister moves
contents.reason: Supports the presentation/group interpretation of the local trefoil comparison. The actual group isomorphism and consistent meridian convention are supplied by the completed local Wirtinger theorem.

contents.name: §4.2, p. 36: the knot-group abelianization is Z because crossing relations identify meridian classes
contents.reason: Explains why the explicit nonabelian S3 quotient comparison carries more information than the common cyclic abelianization. The B counterexample proves its own cyclic-versus-nonabelian distinction.

contents.name: §4.2, p. 36: stated unknot characterization G(K)=Z iff K is the unknot, and general group-isomorphism undecidability
contents.reason: The assigned counterexample uses only an explicit S3 quotient and no global unknot-detection theorem or decision procedure for arbitrary group presentations.

contents.name: §4.2, pp. 36–37: odd-prime Fox colorings as meridian-preserving representations into the dihedral group
contents.reason: Provides a second independent treatment connecting the finite coloring equation with group representations; the local proof directly verifies the S3 images and does not assume a classification result.
